text: About 5.5 billion people used the internet in 2024
as_written: about five and a half billion people were using the internet in 2024
source: International Telecommunication Union, Facts and Figures 2024

text: That is roughly two thirds of humanity
as_written: That is roughly two thirds of humanity
source: International Telecommunication Union, Facts and Figures 2024 (68 percent of the world population online)

text: About 2.6 billion people were offline in 2024
as_written: The other two point six billion or so were offline
source: International Telecommunication Union, Facts and Figures 2024

text: About 99 percent of intercontinental data travels through submarine cables
as_written: about ninety-nine percent of the data that crosses between continents travels through cables on the sea floor
source: TeleGeography; International Cable Protection Committee

text: More than 500 submarine cables are in service
as_written: There are more than five hundred of them in service
source: TeleGeography Submarine Cable Map

text: Light in optical fibre travels at about two thirds of its vacuum speed, roughly 200,000 km per second
as_written: about two thirds of its speed in a vacuum, which is roughly two hundred thousand kilometres every second
source: Standard optical fibre physics (refractive index about 1.47); speed of light defined by the BIPM/SI as 299,792,458 m/s

text: Half of Earth's circumference is about 20,000 km
as_written: about twenty thousand kilometres
source: Earth circumference of about 40,075 km, IAU/NASA Earth fact sheet

text: A signal covering that distance in fibre needs around a tenth of a second
as_written: that takes around a tenth of a second
source: Derived from 20,000 km divided by about 200,000 km/s

text: GPS satellites orbit more than 20,000 km up
as_written: orbit more than twenty thousand kilometres above you
source: GPS.gov, U.S. Space Force (orbital altitude about 20,200 km)

text: GPS satellites broadcast one way and do not receive from user devices
as_written: they only broadcast. They never listen
source: GPS.gov, U.S. Space Force

text: The DNS root has 13 root server addresses run by 12 organisations
as_written: thirteen root server addresses, run by twelve different organisations
source: root-servers.org

text: The root servers are replicated on well over a thousand machines worldwide
as_written: copied onto well over a thousand machines around the world
source: root-servers.org instance count

text: DNS answers are cached for a time set by the name's owner (TTL)
as_written: Those saved copies expire after a time set by whoever owns the name
source: IETF RFC 1035, Domain Names Implementation and Specification

text: The internet comprises tens of thousands of independent networks
as_written: tens of thousands of separate networks
source: Regional Internet Registries / CIDR Report autonomous system counts

text: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp were down about six hours on 4 October 2021
as_written: On the fourth of October 2021, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp disappeared from the internet for about six hours
source: Facebook Engineering, More details about the October 4 outage; Cloudflare blog analysis

text: The cause was a routine maintenance command that withdrew the routes to Facebook's servers
as_written: A routine maintenance command went wrong, and the company's networks stopped telling the rest of the internet where its servers were
source: Facebook Engineering, More details about the October 4 outage; Cloudflare blog analysis

text: Tools engineers use to respond were affected and physical access to data centres slowed the fix
as_written: The tools its engineers normally used to respond to a problem like this were affected by the same fault
source: Facebook Engineering, More details about the October 4 outage

text: Data centres used about 415 terawatt hours in 2024, about 1.5 percent of global electricity
as_written: roughly four hundred and fifteen terawatt hours of electricity in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency, about one and a half percent of the world's electricity
source: International Energy Agency, Energy and AI (2025)

text: About 80 percent of world trade by volume moves by sea
as_written: Roughly eighty percent of world trade by volume moves by sea
source: UNCTAD, Review of Maritime Transport

text: A January 2022 eruption near Tonga broke the country's only submarine cable, leaving it largely offline about five weeks
as_written: Tonga stayed largely cut off from the internet for about five weeks
source: Tonga Cable Ltd; Southern Cross Cable Network reports; Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai eruption of 15 January 2022

text: Egypt's government shut the internet for about five days in 2011
as_written: about five days
source: Reporting by Renesys/Dyn and Arbor Networks on Egypt's shutdown, 28 January to 2 February 2011

text: Andrew Tanenbaum's quip about the bandwidth of a station wagon full of tapes
as_written: never to underestimate the bandwidth of a station wagon full of tapes
source: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, Computer Networks

text: A study had more than 2,000 people deactivate Facebook for four weeks before the 2018 US midterms, finding small wellbeing gains
as_written: economists paid more than two thousand people to deactivate Facebook for four weeks
source: Allcott, Braghieri, Eichmeyer and Gentzkow, The Welfare Effects of Social Media, American Economic Review, 2020

text: The first ARPANET message was sent in October 1969 from UCLA to SRI and crashed after two letters, 'lo'
as_written: In October 1969, a computer at the University of California, Los Angeles tried to send the word login to a computer at the Stanford Research Institute
source: UCLA Samueli School of Engineering history; Computer History Museum

text: The ARPANET had four computers by December 1969
as_written: By December of that year the network had four computers
source: Computer History Museum; Hafner and Lyon, Where Wizards Stay Up Late

text: ARPANET switched to TCP/IP on 1 January 1983
as_written: On the first of January 1983, the ARPANET switched over to the protocols we still use today
source: Internet Society, Brief History of the Internet; IETF RFC 801

text: Paul Baran at RAND studied survivable communications in the early 1960s; whether ARPANET was built for nuclear survival is disputed
as_written: the engineer Paul Baran at the RAND Corporation did study how to build communications that could survive an attack
source: RAND Corporation, On Distributed Communications (1964); Hafner and Lyon, Where Wizards Stay Up Late

text: 38 percent of webpages that existed in 2013 were no longer accessible in 2023
as_written: thirty-eight percent of the pages that existed in 2013 could no longer be reached by 2023
source: Pew Research Center, When Online Content Disappears (May 2024)
